html:
The Belovezha Accords were signed on 8 December 1991 at a hunting lodge in the Białowieża Forest of western Belarus by the leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus, declaring that the Soviet Union no longer existed.

Boris Yeltsin of Russia, Leonid Kravchuk of Ukraine and Stanislav Shushkevich of Belarus met after Ukraine voted for independence. They founded the Commonwealth of Independent States in place of the Union. Gorbachev was left without a state, and other republics joined the Commonwealth at Alma-Ata on 21 December. Four days later Gorbachev resigned and the Soviet Union was dissolved. Belarus became independent with Minsk as the Commonwealth's seat.
sum: The Belovezha Accords were signed on 8 December 1991 at a hunting lodge in the Białowieża Forest of western Belarus by the leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus, declaring that the Soviet Union no longer existed.
